name: Reptile Care Checklist
description: A general reptile care checklist covering enclosure, heating, UVB, humidity, diet and cleaning.

items.text: Research the exact care requirements for your species
items.note: Temperatures, lighting, humidity and diet differ greatly between reptiles

items.text: Confirm adult size and enclosure needs before buying
Find a reptile-experienced veterinarian in your area
Check local laws and permits for the species
Choose an enclosure sized for the adult animal
Use a substrate appropriate to the species
Provide hides on both the warm and cool sides
Add climbing branches, rocks or plants as suited
Supply a clean water source sized for the reptile
Set up a heat source to create a warm-to-cool gradient
Provide UVB lighting if the species requires it
Use thermostats to control heating equipment
items.note: Unregulated heat sources can burn reptiles

items.text: Monitor warm- and cool-side temperatures with accurate gauges
Replace UVB bulbs on schedule as output fades over time
Maintain the humidity range required for the species
Monitor humidity with a hygrometer
Mist or use a humid hide if needed for shedding
Provide ventilation to prevent stagnant, moldy air
Keep day-night light and temperature cycles consistent
Feed the correct diet and prey or plants for the species
Follow an appropriate feeding schedule by age and size
Dust feeder insects with calcium or supplements if advised
Offer correctly sized, safe food items
Remove uneaten live or fresh food promptly
Spot-clean waste and uneaten food daily
Refresh and disinfect the water dish regularly
Do a full substrate change and enclosure clean periodically
Watch shedding, appetite, droppings and behavior
Consult a reptile vet for any sign of illness

faq.q: What does a reptile enclosure need?
faq.a: Most reptiles need a correctly sized enclosure with a heat source creating a warm-to-cool gradient, appropriate UVB lighting for many species, controlled humidity, suitable substrate, hides and clean water. Exact requirements vary by species.

faq.q: Why is UVB and heat so important for reptiles?
faq.a: Reptiles are ectotherms that rely on external heat to digest and stay healthy, and many species need UVB to produce vitamin D3 and absorb calcium. Incorrect temperatures or lighting are leading causes of illness in captive reptiles.

faq.q: How do I know the right temperature and humidity?
faq.a: There is no universal answer — each species has specific ranges. Research your exact reptile's needs and use accurate thermometers and a hygrometer to monitor the warm side, cool side and humidity rather than guessing.

faq.q: When should I see a vet for a reptile?
faq.a: This checklist is general guidance. Consult a reptile-experienced veterinarian for any change in appetite, behavior, skin, breathing or droppings, and research species-specific health and diet needs before bringing a reptile home.

faq.q: Can I print this reptile care checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF so you can keep it near the enclosure and tick off daily and routine tasks.
